scientific_name: Erwinia carotovora subsp. carotovora, Erwinia chrysanthemi and related bacteria
description: A bacterial disease that causes soft, watery rot of bulbs in onion and other Allium crops. It often appears near harvest or during storage and produces a foul-smelling decay.
symptoms: Young leaves become pale, bleached and wilted
Soft watery rot of bulb scales
Entire bulb becomes soft and rotten
Bad-smelling viscous fluid oozing from the neck of bulbs
management: Avoid injuries during planting and harvest
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead irrigation
Allow onion tops to mature before harvest
Store bulbs at low temperature and moderate humidity
biological_control: Encourage beneficial soil microbes through organic matter management
Use biological control agents such as Bacillus-based biofungicides
Improve soil health to suppress bacterial pathogens
chemical_control: Copper-based bactericides such as copper hydroxide
Copper sprays applied regularly to slow disease development
prevention: Plant certified pathogen-free bulbs or seeds
Store bulbs at about 4°C with 65–70% relative humidity
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization and maintain adequate calcium levels
source: Van der Wolf & Duriat – Soft rot diseases in Allium
